# AArch32 signal frame, measured on the device (do not edit; regenerate with tests/corpus/sigframe_probe.c)
#
# Why: C26's delivery must synthesise the frame a kernel would have made. docs/research/02 §5.4 calls this
# the "ugly part" and says to verify the layout against the kernel headers rather than recall it. This file
# is the measurement instead of the recollection: the probe installs a handler, has a helper thread interrupt
# it with tkill, and hunts the interrupted PC/SP inside the `ucontext` the kernel handed the handler.
#
# generated by: tests/corpus/sigframe_probe.c, built as armv7 and run on the device below.
# device=SM-X710 serial=R52Y106BECZ abilist32=armeabi-v7a,armeabi sdk=36
# compiler: clang --target=armv7-none-linux-androideabi26 -mthumb -mfloat-abi=softfp -mfpu=neon -Os -static
# consumed by: core/runtime/signal_frame.h (the offsets below are the ones delivery writes)

# --- sizes (measured, printed by the probe)
sizeof(siginfo_t)          128
sizeof(ucontext_t)         744
sizeof(stack_t)            12
rt_sigframe (info+uc)      872
measured frame from SP     880        # interrupted_sp - (info address): 0xffd2c4c8 - 0xffd2c158 = 0x370

# --- the handler's arguments, measured
handler(sig, info, ucontext):  info = ucontext - 128   # 0xffd2c158 vs 0xffd2c1d8: sizeof(siginfo_t)

# --- ucontext_t offsets, confirmed against the interrupted values
uc_flags                   0
uc_link                    4
uc_stack.ss_sp             8
uc_stack.ss_flags          12
uc_stack.ss_size           16
uc_mcontext                20         # struct sigcontext
uc_sigmask                 104        # bionic sigset_t (4) + __padding_rt_sigset (4)
__padding                  112        # 120 bytes, glibc-sigset_t padding
uc_regspace                232        # 512 bytes, VFP/legacy frame (left zero by delivery)
total                      744

# --- struct sigcontext offsets (absolute in ucontext, and relative to uc_mcontext)
trap_no                    abs 20     rel 0
error_code                 abs 24     rel 4
oldmask                    abs 28     rel 8
arm_r0                     abs 32     rel 12
arm_r1                     abs 36     rel 16
arm_r2                     abs 40     rel 20
arm_r3                     abs 44     rel 24
arm_r4                     abs 48     rel 28
arm_r5                     abs 52     rel 32
arm_r6                     abs 56     rel 36
arm_r7                     abs 60     rel 40
arm_r8                     abs 64     rel 44
arm_r9                     abs 68     rel 48
arm_r10                    abs 72     rel 52
arm_fp   (r11)             abs 76     rel 56
arm_ip   (r12)             abs 80     rel 60
arm_sp                     abs 84     rel 64     # measured: 0xffd2c4c8 == interrupted SP
arm_lr                     abs 88     rel 68     # measured: 0x0001b029
arm_pc                     abs 92     rel 72     # measured: 0x0001b1a4 (probe recorded 0x0001b198 inside its loop)
arm_cpsr                   abs 96     rel 76     # measured: 0x60840030 — bit 5 (T) set, as -mthumb requires
fault_address              abs 100    rel 80
sigcontext size            84

# --- a note on the two false positives the probe reports, so nobody re-derives them
# "ucontext+40 = interrupted PC": +40 is arm_r2, which the `mov %0, pc` idiom left holding the address. The
#   real arm_pc is +92, a few instructions on from the recorded value (the loop, not the mov, was interrupted).
# "ucontext+44 and +732 = interrupted SP": +44 is arm_r3, and +732 falls inside uc_regspace. Only +84 is arm_sp.

# --- flags seen in the guests themselves (not the probe)
# libmono installs sig 30 (SIGPWR, its GC thread-suspend) with flags 0x14000000 = SA_RESTART|SA_RESTORER and
# restorer 0x1a7240 — AArch32 requires SA_RESTORER, as docs/research/02 §5.4 predicted. Its handler is at
# libmono.so+0x2bdb59. The 16-byte sigaction the guest passes reads {handler, flags, restorer, mask[2]}:
# measured `rt_sigaction(sig=30)` act: +0=0x5fab59 +4=0x14000000 +8=0x1a7240 +12=0xffffbfd9.
